key: And she said: ‘The glory is departed from Israel; for the ark of God is taken.’
s: Dying in childbirth at the news from the battle, Phinehas’ wife speaks a second time; Radak, on 4:22, reads the repetition as naming the ark alone, the chief of the glory, where the first saying also counted her husband and his father.

evidence.gloss: She said it another time: at first she said the glory was exiled because of the ark that was captured and because her father-in-law and her husband had died; now she said again that the glory was exiled because of the ark alone, for it is the chief of the glory.

reason: verse.js ok, ref 1 Samuel 4:22 and at [235,22] match. Plain sense faithful: 4:19 to 4:21 give the tidings of the battle, her labour and her naming of Ichabod with the first saying; 4:20 has her at the point of death; 4:22 is her second saying; no four-word run from the verse. Opened the packet on 4:21 and 4:22 (Rashi has nothing on 4:22, only glosses on 4:21; Metzudat David on 4:22 says the same in brief; no Midrash Rabbah on 1 Samuel). Radak on 4:22 contrasts the first saying (ark plus father-in-law and husband) with the second (the ark alone, the chief of the glory): the sentence stays within his words.
